Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Om Prakash Pandey
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Ajay Bhanot,J.

By means of the bail application the applicant has prayed to be enlarged on bail in Case Crime No.135 of 2018 at Police Station-Lalapur, District-Prayagraj under Sections 498A, 304B IPC and 3/4 of the D.P. Act.
The applicant is in jail since 01.11.2018.
The bail application of the applicant was rejected by the learned trial court on 15.09.2022.

The following arguments made by Shri Nigamendra Shukla, learned counsel holding brief of Shri Om Prakash Pandey, learned counsel on behalf of the applicant, which could not be satisfactorily refuted by Shri Rishi Chaddha, learned AGA from the record, entitle the applicant for grant of bail:
1. The applicant is the husband of the deceased.

sentences.text: 2. The applicant and the deceased had harmonious relationship.
3. The applicant never harassed the deceased nor did he demand dowry.
4. The prosecution witnesses namely first informant (father of the deceased) and mother of the deceased have repudiated the prosecution case before the learned trial court.
The said witnesses have declared hostile by the learned trial court at the instance of the prosecution.
5. The prerequisites of Section 304-B of the IPC are not established before the trial court.
Hence, the burden of proof shall not be reversed.
6. The deceased died of burn injuries sustained in a cooking accident.
7. The applicant is a daily labour who was not at the place of incident when the accident occurred.
8. The applicant was informed about the incident by fellow villagers and his family members.
He promptly rushed home and informed the police authorities.
9. The applicant is a law abiding citizen who cooperated in enquiry and has joined the trial proceedings.
10. The trial is moving at a snail's pace and shows no signs of an early conclusion.
The applicant is not responsible for the delay in the trial proceedings.
11. Inordinate delay in concluding trial has lead to an indefinite detention of the applicant.
Right of the applicant to a speedy trial has been violated.
12. The applicant does not have any criminal history apart from this case.
13. The applicant is not a flight risk.
The applicant being a law abiding citizen has always cooperated with the investigation and undertakes to cooperate with the court proceedings.
There is no possibility of his influencing witnesses, tampering with the evidence or reoffending.
In the light of the preceding discussion and without making any observations on the merits of the case, the bail application is allowed.
Let the applicant-Ramesh Chandra be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number, on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court below.
The following conditions be imposed in the interest of justice:-
